items.prompt: One way to find the area of an L-shaped figure is to:

choices.A: Enclose it in one large rectangle, then subtract the missing piece
choices.B: Multiply all the side lengths together at once

items.rationale: The enclose-and-subtract method surrounds the shape with a rectangle and removes the extra area.

items.prompt: A large rectangle measures 12 by 10 (area 120). A 4-by-3 rectangular corner (area 12) is missing to form an L-shape. What is the area of the L-shaped figure?
An L-shape is decomposed into Rectangle 1 (6 by 5) and Rectangle 2 (3 by 4). What is the total area?
For a trickier T-shaped figure, which strategy works?

choices.C: Either enclose-and-subtract or decompose-and-add can work, depending on the shape

items.rationale: Both strategies are valid tools; which one is easiest depends on how the figure is shaped.

items.prompt: A T-shaped figure is split into two rectangles: one 8 by 3, and one 2 by 6. What is the total area?
